name: Leonardo da Vinci
bio: Italian polymath and painter whose studies of anatomy, light, engineering, and nature shaped the ideal of the Renaissance artist. His paintings are known for subtle modeling, psychological presence, and experimental composition.

name: Michelangelo Buonarroti
bio: Florentine sculptor, painter, architect, and poet. Michelangelo brought monumental anatomy and dramatic spiritual force to Renaissance art, from the Sistine Chapel ceiling to marble figures such as David.

name: Raphael
bio: Italian painter and architect celebrated for clarity, balanced composition, and graceful figures. Raphael's Vatican frescoes became defining examples of High Renaissance harmony.

name: Sandro Botticelli
bio: Florentine painter associated with lyrical line, mythological scenes, and refined devotional works. His Birth of Venus and Primavera helped define the poetic visual language of early Renaissance Florence.

name: Titian
bio: Venetian master whose rich color, loose handling, and confident portraiture influenced European painting for centuries. Titian's work bridged Renaissance ideals with a more sensual painterly approach.

name: Caravaggio
bio: Revolutionary painter who brought dramatic chiaroscuro and gritty realism to sacred subjects. His intense lighting and visceral human figures changed the course of European painting.

name: Rembrandt van Rijn
bio: Dutch master of light, shadow, and human psychology. His portraits, self-portraits, and biblical scenes remain unmatched in their emotional depth and technical brilliance.

name: Johannes Vermeer
bio: Dutch painter famed for his serene domestic interiors bathed in cool northern light. His meticulous technique and quiet intimacy make every scene feel like a private moment frozen in time.

name: Peter Paul Rubens
bio: Flemish painter known for dynamic movement, lush color, and exuberant compositions. His large-scale altarpieces and mythological scenes defined the Baroque visual language.

name: Gian Lorenzo Bernini
bio: Sculptor, architect, and painter who gave marble the appearance of living flesh. His works in Rome, including the Ecstasy of Saint Teresa, embody Baroque theatricality.

name: Caspar David Friedrich
bio: German Romantic painter whose misty landscapes and solitary wanderers evoke spiritual longing and the sublime power of nature. Wanderer above the Sea of Fog became an icon of Romanticism.

name: J. M. W. Turner
bio: British painter whose luminous, atmospheric seascapes and landscapes dissolved form into pure light and color. Turner paved the way for Impressionism and modern abstraction.

name: Eugène Delacroix
bio: French Romantic painter whose explosive color and energetic brushwork challenged the calm classicism of his era. Liberty Leading the People remains a symbol of revolutionary spirit.

name: Claude Monet
bio: French Impressionist who painted light itself rather than objects. His series of water lilies, haystacks, and Rouen Cathedral capture fleeting moments in vibrating color.

name: Vincent van Gogh
bio: Dutch painter whose bold, swirling brushstrokes and intense color expressed deep emotion. In just a decade he created some of the most recognizable images in art history.

name: Edgar Degas
bio: French painter and sculptor celebrated for his compositions of dancers, racehorses, and bathers. Degas combined classical draftsmanship with modern, off-center viewpoints.

name: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
bio: French Impressionist painter of radiant light, warm flesh tones, and joyful social scenes. Renoir's touch remained gentle even as his style evolved toward classical form.

name: Pablo Picasso
bio: Spanish painter and sculptor who shattered perspective with Cubism. Picasso's restless experimentation across decades—from Blue Period to Guernica—made him the most influential artist of the 20th century.

name: Wassily Kandinsky
bio: Russian painter and theorist credited with creating the first purely abstract artworks. Kandinsky believed color and form could express spiritual truths without depicting reality.

name: Salvador Dalí
bio: Spanish Surrealist whose meticulously painted dreamscapes—melting clocks, burning giraffes—explored the unconscious mind with hallucinatory precision.

name: Frida Kahlo
bio: Mexican painter whose intensely personal self-portraits blended realism with symbolism, indigenous culture, and raw emotional honesty. Her work became a global icon of identity and resilience.
